content.title: Man arrested at Trump National Golf Club with weapons and body armor
content.text: Rory McIlroy's latest Masters triumph has not only added another prestigious title to his career but has also delivered a major financial boost to those working closest with him. While the Northern Irish golfer celebrated his sixth major championship, attention has also turned to his long-time caddie Harry Diamond, who is set to receive a significant payday following the win at Augusta National. To watch this video, agree to share video information with third partiesAgree|More infoTheir partnership, built on years of trust and history, once again proved decisive on one of golf's biggest stages.Diamond has been McIlroy's caddie since 2017, stepping in after JP Fitzgerald's long spell on the bag. However, their relationship stretches far beyond professional sport. The two have known each other since childhood, first meeting at Holywood Golf Club in Northern Ireland. That familiarity has often been credited as a key strength in their working relationship, particularly under pressure at major tournaments.Following his victory, McIlroy collected $4.5 million in prize money, taking his total career earnings to an estimated $114.7 million. Under the widely used arrangement in professional golf, caddies typically earn around 10 percent of a player's winnings. Based on that structure, Diamond is expected to take home at least $450,000 for his role in the triumph. While that figure is modest compared to McIlroy's overall fortune, it represents a life-changing sum earned through a single tournament week.A partnership built on trust and historyMcIlroy has frequently highlighted the personal bond he shares with Diamond, describing him as far more than just a bag carrier. Their connection, rooted in years of friendship, has helped them navigate the emotional and technical demands of elite competition. McIlroy has previously said Diamond has been "like a big brother" throughout his life, reflecting the deep level of trust between them and the stability it brings during high-pressure moments on the course.Their success at Augusta National also carries historical weight. McIlroy became only the fourth player ever to win back-to-back Masters titles, further elevating his place in the sport's record books. For both player and caddie, the achievement represents more than just another tournament victory.As McIlroy continues to build on an already remarkable career, Diamond remains a constant presence.
